conflict_topics: who takes the seat when it becomes free
dialogue_quality_notes: Speakers used concise, natural requests and justifications (e.g., packet as reservation vs bowl risk of spilling).
Some needless repetition from Agent B ('I'll let you know when I'm done.') across rounds 6–7.
No role confusion; statements remain consistent with the physical constraints (fixed stools, full hawker centre).
evaluation.final_reason: Agent A withdrew their immediate demand for the seat in Turn 3: 'Fine — I'll take another seat this time.' B continued to occupy the seat and said they would 'let you know when I'm done' (Turn 8), and D agreed to wait. The active contest over taking the seat right then ended because Agent A relinquished the demand.
position_change_notes: Agent A shifted from asserting entitlement (Turn 1) to withdrawing the demand (Turn 3): 'Fine — I'll take another seat this time.'

Agent B retained the practical position of staying and finishing their meal, repeatedly promising to notify others when done ('I will let you know when I'm done.' / 'I'll let you know when I'm done.').
Agent D moved from a bystander to an acknowledged waitlist position, stating intent to take the seat when free (Turn 5, Turn 18).

round_scores.evidence: Turn 1 — Agent A: 'Agent B, I left that tissue packet to save this seat. Please move it — I need to sit, my food's hot.' vs Turn 2 — Agent B: 'That tissue packet wasn't a reservation — it was unattended, so I sat in good faith. My bowl's open and will spill if I try to carry it. Wait until I finish or take another seat.' (direct incompatible claims over entitlement to the seat)

Turn 3 — Agent A: 'Fine — I'll take another seat this time. Don't move my things again without asking; I left that packet to save the spot.' (Agent A withdraws immediate demand) and Turn 5 — Agent D: 'Agent A — I saw you leave that tissue packet earlier. If that seat frees up, I'll take it.' (no direct challenge to B; conflict over immediate seating is defused)
Turn 6 — Agent A: 'Alright — take it if it frees up.' and Turn 7 — Agent D: 'I'll take it when it frees up.' (no contesting statements; acceptance of the de-escalation)
Turn 8 — Agent B: 'Okay — I'll finish here. I will let you know when I'm done.' (B indicates intention to notify; no ongoing dispute)
[No public speech or observable action recorded]

Turn 18 — Agent D: 'Okay — I'll wait here. I'll take the seat when it's free.' and Turn 19 — Agent B: 'Okay


I'll let you know when I'm done.' (both accept the waiting arrangement)
Turn 23 — Agent B: 'Okay — I'll let you know when I'm done.' and Turn 27 — Agent B: 'Okay — I'll let you know when I'm done.' (repeated confirmation; no contest)
[No public speech or observable action recorded]

substantive_insights: Core tension was a norm/fact dispute: whether a small tissue packet legitimately reserved a seat versus B's claim of good-faith occupation.
B invoked a practical constraint (open bowl that might spill) as a reason not to move immediately, which reduced pressure for an immediate concession.
Resolution occurred via withdrawal of the claimant (A), not via B conceding or a negotiated exchange.
